GainsBlock.rationale: `public override bool GainsBlock => true` (ToricToughness.cs:17) == the class attribute.

ctor.rationale: `base(2, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Event, TargetType.Self)` (ToricToughness.cs:27-30) == cost 2 / SKILL / EVENT / SELF.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DynamicVar("Turns", 2m)` + `new BlockVar(5m, ValueProp.Move)` (ToricToughness.cs:19-23) == both numbers, both declared. Move without Unpowered -> POWERED block, so NOT in gap G1's blast radius.

OnPlay.rationale: `decimal blockAmount = await CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.Block, cardPlay);` then `(await PowerCmd.Apply<ToricToughnessPower>(..., DynamicVars["Turns"].BaseValue, ...))?.SetBlock(blockAmount)` (ToricToughness.cs:34-35) == `gained = BlockCmd.apply(...)` then apply the power and `power.set_block(gained)`. The load-bearing detail is that the power carries the block ACTUALLY GAINED rather than the printed 5 -- so Vambrace's doubling or Frail's reduction propagates into the next two turns' regain -- and the sim threads `BlockCmd.apply`'s return value through in exactly the same way. The Turns value is the power's AMOUNT and the block is set separately, the same two-step shape as card/the_bomb. Presentation, folded in: the Block hover tip (25).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Block.UpgradeValueBy(2m)` (ToricToughness.cs:40) == `self._block += 2` (5 -> 7). The Turns var stays 2 when upgraded on both sides.

guards.what: C# skips SetBlock when Apply returns NULL via `?.`; the sim re-fetches by id and skips on None (ToricToughness.cs:35 vs event_cards.py:147-149)
guards.issue: Same mechanism and same verdict as card/crimson_mantle's and card/inferno's guards (rule 3): `PowerCmd.Apply<T>` returns null when combat is ending, when `!target.CanReceivePowers`, or when a stacking `ModifyAmount` resolves to 0 (PowerCmd.cs:29-34, 68-87), and the sim's re-fetch cannot distinguish those from a successful apply -- so a second Toric Toughness whose amount was zeroed would still overwrite the stored block. DORMANT: no ported effect modifies a positive self-applied buff down to exactly 0 (Artifact intercepts only debuffs, cmds.py:299-306), and the other two null cases imply the combat is over. This is the third of the pool's three `?.`-after-Apply sites.
